item.title: The full shadow of a polynomial II. Vanishing root masses and holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex polynomial $P$, its full shadow is the closure of the set of zeros of all derivatives of all powers $P^n$, and its limiting core is the Hausdorff limit, as $n\to\infty$, of the set of zeros of all derivatives of $P^n$. These sets retain geometric information that weak limits of root-counting measures discard. We determine complete zero-set limits for arrays of polynomials whose roots approach finitely many locations. A cluster containing $o(D)$ roots of a degree-$D$ polynomial can survive outside the limiting support of the derivative zeros, which depends only on the positive limiting masses: under repeated differentiation, the zeros it produces follow a straight path, selected by an explicit min--max condition, and preserve the cluster's exact multiplicity. When such a location instead carries a small positive mass $\varepsilon$, the support of the limiting zero distribution at a fixed ratio of derivative order to degree develops an arc on the $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ scale with a universal local semicircle profile. We use these mechanisms to prove that polynomial shadows can have robust and arbitrarily complicated topology. For every $k\ge2$, there are polynomials with $k+2$ distinct root locations whose limiting cores and full shadows have at least $\binom{k}{2}$ holes; this persists under coefficient perturbations and among square-free polynomials without a reflection axis. In a four-location family, the core and full-shadow areas tend to zero while one hole has area tending to $8/1221$.
item.dc:creator: Christian H\"agg, Boris Shapiro

item.title: Some properties of completely convex functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the class $CC_\alpha$ of completely convex functions of order $\alpha$, defined through a two-point analogous of the classical convexity condition. We give several equivalent characterizations of $CC_\alpha$, together with representation formulas in terms of two auxiliary Schwarz functions linked by a compatibility equation. From these representations, we derive coefficient bounds, a subordination result $zf'/f$, and a two-point Taylor expansion in which the Schwarzian derivative $S_f$ arises naturally as the coefficient of the linear term. This yields a pointwise bound for $S_f$ and a bound for the pre-Schwarzian norm $\|P_f\|_{CC_\alpha}$, improving the classical Yamashita bound when $\alpha\leq 1-1/\sqrt2 $. We also show that, unlike the class $C_\alpha$ of convex functions of order $\alpha$, every $f\in CC_\alpha$ is bounded when $\alpha>0$.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Arbel\'aez, Rodrigo Hern\'andez

item.title: A reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and its extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study reciprocal moments of the critical points of a polynomial with a simple zero at the origin. A positive similarity transforms a reciprocal derivative companion into a complex symmetric matrix. This gives a short proof of the reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and a refinement for every elementary symmetric function. We determine the optimal constants in the corresponding inequalities for every positive exponent, including the sublinear range, and extend the results to arbitrary positive charges. We also characterize the normal powers of the companion and of its symmetric representative. The resulting criterion gives the complete equality cases in two quartic inequalities and explains the appearance of noncollinear equality configurations at higher orders. We also obtain a closed generating determinant and a quantitative collinearity estimate.
item.dc:creator: Olga Holtz

item.title: Truncated Dirichlet estimates for Bloch functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the truncated Dirichlet functional \[ \Phi_n (f) = \sum_{k = 1}^n k |a_k|^2, \quad f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^\infty a_k z^k, \] when $f$ belongs to the Bloch space. If $n \geq 27$, we find a normalized Bloch function $f_n$ such that \[ \Phi_n (f_n) > n B_n^2, \] where $B_n = \max \{ |a_n| : \| f \|_{\mathcal{B}} = 1 \}$, thus proving that an inequality by Kayumov and Wirths cannot be extended to large values of $n$. Nevertheless, we show that the inequality $\Phi_n(f) \leq n B_n^2$ holds for all normalized functions when $n \leq 9$.
item.dc:creator: Iason Efraimidis, Adri\'an Llinares, Alejandro Mas

item.title: Holomorphic functions and hulls of Matsuki-dual orbits of $SU(p,q)$ in complex Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.41828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G_0$ be a real form of a complex semisimple group acting on a flag manifold $Z$, with maximal compact subgroup $K_0$ and its complexification $K$. Matsuki duality pairs each $G_0$-orbit $\gamma$ with a $K$-orbit $\kappa$, and $M=\kappa\cap\gamma$ is a compact $K_0$-orbit. For lower-dimensional $\gamma$, $M$ is a compact CR manifold, and we ask which functions are holomorphic near $M$ and what its holomorphic hull is. In general, we show that $K_0$-finite holomorphic functions near $M$ are regular functions on $K$-orbits, and that $M$ carries non-constant holomorphic germs if some $K$-stable prime divisor of $Z$ misses $\kappa$, and, under a connectedness hypothesis, only constants otherwise. For $G_0=SU(p,q)$ acting on any Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{p+q})$ we give a complete answer. Holomorphic functions near $M$ are constant unless $M$ is of holomorphic type: $k\in\{p,q\}$ and $M$ lies in the Harish-Chandra chart of the bounded symmetric domain $\mathcal{D}$. Then $M$ is the manifold of rank-$c$ partial isometries, and a holomorphic hull of $M$ is $\overline{\mathcal{D}}\cap\{\mathrm{rank}\le c\}$. This agrees with the polynomial hull of Kaup and Zaitsev except in one totally real case, where it is strictly smaller because $\det^{-1}$ is holomorphic near $U(p)$. The same dichotomy decides when global CR functions on $M$ are constant and when holomorphic sections of line bundles near $M$ are global; its exceptions differ from the Gindikin-Matsuki exceptions for cycle spaces, except at the base point of $\mathcal{D}$. This settles the descent question left open in earlier work with K. Shabbir on rank-one orbits. We also determine which $K$-orbits carry non-constant regular functions, prove constancy via chains of rational curves for small $c$, and compute Levi forms in examples.
item.dc:creator: Irfan Ullah

item.title: A four-dimensional residue calculus for quaternionic slice regular functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a 4-dimensional residue calculus for quaternionic slice semiregular functions. Its local singularities are isolated real poles and 2-dimensional spheres. For the latter, we introduce a spherical residue and characterize it as a spherical Laurent coefficient, as the sum of two classical residues on any full complex slice, and by a finite differential procedure involving alternating spherical and slice derivatives. The residue theorem expresses a weighted boundary flux on a circular domain as the sum of the real and spherical residues it contains. Beyond this formula, polynomially weighted flux moments recover every coefficient of every finite principal part, including the companion coefficient at a spherical pole, invisible to ordinary residue summation. Once the polar components and order bounds are fixed, the quotient of the real polynomial ring by the global pole polynomial is the finite-dimensional algebra of weights. We prove that the residue pairing is well defined and nondegenerate, and identifies formal principal parts with the full quaternion-valued real dual of this algebra. Hermite interpolation and the Chinese remainder theorem provide global weights selecting each local coefficient. We separate the regularity domain of the function from the geometry of integration: for a smooth noncircular integration domain compactly contained in a circular ambient domain, away from the reals and with boundary disjoint from the polar set, we establish an exact residue formula with an explicit volume correction governed by the Cauchy-Fueter operator. The theory includes higher-order poles, exceptional points, product domains, and zero divisors. Applications give formulas for rational and oscillatory integrals on the imaginary hyperplane and characterize the rational data on the 3-dimensional imaginary subspace of the quaternions admitting a canonical slice regular extension.
item.dc:creator: Amedeo Altavilla

item.title: Algebraic Vector Fields of Connected Semi-simple Matrix Groups are 3-generated
item.description: arXiv:2610.41201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields for any connected, semi-simple matrix group over $\mathbb{F}$, for $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$, can be generated by three $\mathbb{F}$-complete algebraic vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Jiang, Xudong Chen

item.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.41237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$. The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.
item.dc:creator: Kiwamu Watanabe

item.title: The metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4
item.description: arXiv:2610.41954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a counterexample to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4. Here, we prove that the metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture is true in dimension 4. More precisely, let $f,g\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be germs of reduced holomorphic functions, and let $\varphi\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism such that $\varphi(V(f))=V(g)$. We prove that if every irreducible component of the tangent cone of $V(f)$ at the origin has a singular locus of dimension at most two, then $V(f)$ and $V(g)$ have the same multiplicity at the origin. In particular, the multiplicity of complex analytic hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\leq 4$, is an embedded bi-Lipschitz invariant; the cases $n=2$ and $n=3$ were known. This extends a previous result of the author for tangent cones whose components have singular loci of dimension at most one. We also prove that two irreducible homogeneous hypersurfaces whose singular loci have dimension at most two, and which are mapped onto each other by a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{C}^n$ fixing the origin, have the same degree.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio

item.title: A new strong rigidity phenomenon for the Bergman metric
item.description: arXiv:2608.15998v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a new local-to-global rigidity phenomenon for the Bergman metric. Namely, under natural geometric hypotheses, a local conformal identification of Bergman metrics determines the underlying complex manifold globally, up to the unavoidable ambiguity of removing Bergman-negligible subsets. More precisely, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain with a complete Bergman metric, and suppose that the Bergman metric of a complex manifold $M$ is locally conformal, via a holomorphic map $f$, to that of $\Omega$, with a constant conformal factor when $n=1$. We prove that the given local map $f$ extends to a biholomorphism $F\colon M\to D$ onto a subdomain $D\subseteq\Omega$ in two complementary settings. If $M$ is Stein, then $\Omega\setminus D$ is a closed pluripolar set. If $M$ is a bounded domain and $\Omega$ satisfies a natural symmetry condition expressed in terms of its automorphism orbits, then $\Omega\setminus D$ is Bergman-negligible. In particular, this applies when $\Omega$ is a bounded homogeneous domain and yields a characterization, up to Bergman-negligible sets, of a class of bounded domains with locally symmetric Bergman metrics, addressing a question raised by Loi--Palmieri and Zimmer. A key ingredient in the proofs is a new Calabi-type extension theorem tailored to Bergman metrics.
item.dc:creator: Peter Ebenfelt, John N. Treuer, Ming Xiao

item.title: Matrix-valued regular functions of a quaternionic variable - a decomposition and some approximation results
item.description: arXiv:2510.07866v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A quaternionic matrix-valued regular function is a map $F: \Omega \rightarrow M_n(\mathbb{H})$ whose entries are (left) regular functions of a quaternionic variable, where $\Omega$ is a domain in $\mathbb{H}$. Given any $n \times n$ matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ over $\mathbb{H}$ having norm at most $1$, we derive a decomposition of $F(q)$ in the form $U \star \begin{bmatrix} ||F(q_0)|| & 0\\0 & G(q)\end{bmatrix} V$ for some constant unitary matrices $U, V$, some vector $q_0$ and an $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix-valued regular function $G(q)$, where $\star$ denotes the star product over $\mathbb{H}$. We use this to prove a Fisher-type approximation result for matrix-valued regular functions $F(q)$ on the quaternionic unit ball $\mathbb{B}$: if $F(q)$ has norm at most $1$ and is continuous on the boundary of the ball, then $F(q)$ can be uniformly approximated by a convex combination of matrix-valued rational unitary functions on $\overline{\mathbb{B}}$.
item.dc:creator: T. P. Dhashna, Sachindranath Jayaraman

item.title: The edge case of the Hilbert matrix operator between weighted Bergman spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.00252v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Hilbert matrix operator $H$ is bounded on the standard weighted Bergman spaces $A^p_\alpha,\, p>\alpha+2>1$. We examine the limiting case when $\alpha=p-2$, and for $p\leq 2$, we characterize the logarithmic modification of the standard weight needed for the domain $A^p_{v_{\gamma,p}}$ and codomain $A^p_{v_{\beta,p}}$ to ensure boundedness. In particular, we prove that $H:A^2_{\log^\gamma} \to A^2_{\log^\beta}$ is bounded if and only if $\gamma-\beta\geq 2$ and $\gamma>1$, solving an open problem posed by B. Karapetrovi\'c and M. Jevti\'c. We also settle the situation for $p>2$ in all cases, except when the logarithmic exponents $\gamma$ and $\beta$ satisfy $\gamma-\beta=p$. Moreover, we completely solve the same problem when the domain and codomain are certain weighted reflexive $\ell^p$ spaces. All results are extended to the generalized Hilbert operator $H_g$.
item.dc:creator: David Norrbo
